topics.name: Confidentiality, integrity and availability
notes: Confidentiality limits disclosure to authorized recipients.
Integrity protects against unauthorized change or destruction.
Availability concerns timely, reliable access.

lessons.t: Confidentiality, integrity and availability
idea: Confidentiality limits disclosure to authorized recipients.
Integrity protects against unauthorized change or destruction.
Availability concerns timely, reliable access.
recipe: Read the scenario and identify the relevant facts.
Apply the principle to this situation.
Explain why the alternatives do not fit.
oops: Assuming a practice score proves readiness for an official assessment.

steps.text: A university portal stores student schedules.
An outsider reads a private schedule: confidentiality is affected.
Someone changes a classroom without permission: integrity is affected.
Students cannot reach the portal: availability is affected.

bank.q: An outsider reads a private student record. Which property is directly lost?
bank.why: The failure is unauthorized disclosure.

bank.q: A stored invoice amount is changed without approval. Which property is directly affected?
bank.why: The content has been altered without authorization.

bank.q: A service outage prevents authorized customers from checking their accounts. Which goal is directly affected?
bank.why: The service cannot be accessed when needed.

bank.q: Which scenario primarily illustrates an integrity failure?
c: An attacker changes a saved bank routing number
An outsider reads a private memo
A power outage takes a site offline
A legitimate user forgets a password
bank.why: The stored value was changed without authorization.

bank.q: A portal is reachable, but its saved grades have been secretly altered. Which conclusion fits?
c: Availability alone does not establish integrity
Reachability proves the grades are correct
Integrity and availability mean the same thing
bank.why: Being online does not prove that stored values are unmodified.

bank.q: A backup restores access after a disk failure. Which CIA goal does restored access support?
bank.why: Restoring access supports availability; it does not by itself prove other protections.

topics.name: Identity, permissions and audit records
notes: Authentication verifies a claimed identity.
Authorization determines permitted actions.
Audit records support accountability.
Use only the privileges needed for assigned work.
gloss: Only the access needed for assigned duties

lessons.t: Identity, permissions and audit records
idea: Authentication verifies a claimed identity.
Authorization determines permitted actions.
Audit records support accountability.
Use only the privileges needed for assigned work.
recipe: Read the scenario and identify the relevant facts.
Apply the principle to this situation.
Explain why the alternatives do not fit.
oops: Assuming a practice score proves readiness for an official assessment.

steps.text: A staff member signs in to a document service.
The service verifies the identity claim: authentication.
A permission check allows viewing but denies editing: authorization.
An activity record records the action for later review.

bank.q: A system verifies that a user controls a registered authenticator. Which process is this?
bank.why: The system is checking the identity claim.

bank.q: A signed-in user is denied permission to edit a file. Which decision is being enforced?
bank.why: Permissions determine allowed actions after sign-in.

bank.q: A log records who accessed a file and when. Which AAA function does this support?
bank.why: Accounting records activity for later accountability.

bank.q: A temporary intern only needs to read one project folder. Which permission fits least privilege?
c: Write access to every shared folder
bank.why: The requested scope matches the assigned work.

bank.q: A successful login is followed by a failed permission check. Which statement fits?
c: A verified identity may still lack permission
bank.why: Authentication and authorization answer different questions.

bank.q: Which evidence best helps trace a file change to an account?
c: A protected audit record of the change
bank.why: Audit records support tracing actions; their protection matters.

topics.name: Planning and controlling changes
notes: Review security impact before changing a system.
Test changes and obtain appropriate approval.
Prepare a backout plan and update documentation.
gloss: Review of likely effects before a change
Planned return to the previous working state
Scheduled period for planned system work

lessons.t: Planning and controlling changes
idea: Review security impact before changing a system.
Test changes and obtain appropriate approval.
Prepare a backout plan and update documentation.
recipe: Read the scenario and identify the relevant facts.
Apply the principle to this situation.
Explain why the alternatives do not fit.
oops: Assuming a practice score proves readiness for an official assessment.

steps.text: A team plans a firewall rule change.
Identify dependent services and test expected access.
Obtain approval and prepare the previous configuration for rollback.
After the change, validate behavior and update the recorded configuration.

bank.q: Before a firewall change, a team checks which services could stop working. What is this?
bank.why: It evaluates the expected effects of the planned change.

bank.q: A new configuration breaks an essential service. Which prepared document guides returning to the previous state?
bank.why: A backout plan describes recovery from an unsuccessful change.

bank.q: A tested change is ready. What should happen before its planned deployment under change control?
bank.why: Approval is part of a managed change process.

bank.q: Why record a firewall configuration change?
c: So the documented state matches the managed system
bank.why: Accurate records support later operation and review.

bank.q: Which action best tests whether an approved change achieved its intended result?
bank.why: Approval alone does not demonstrate that the deployed change works.

bank.q: Why identify application dependencies before a service restart?
c: To assess effects on connected components
bank.why: A restart can affect dependent services as well as the changed component.

topics.name: Encryption and digital signatures
notes: Encryption transforms readable data into ciphertext.
Symmetric encryption uses a shared secret key.
Public-key cryptography uses paired public and private keys.
A digital signature supports integrity and origin authentication. A signature alone does not hide a message.
gloss: Encryption using a shared secret key
Cryptographic evidence supporting origin and integrity

lessons.t: Encryption and digital signatures
idea: Encryption transforms readable data into ciphertext.
Symmetric encryption uses a shared secret key.
Public-key cryptography uses paired public and private keys.
A digital signature supports integrity and origin authentication. A signature alone does not hide a message.
recipe: Read the scenario and identify the relevant facts.
Apply the principle to this situation.
Explain why the alternatives do not fit.
oops: Assuming a practice score proves readiness for an official assessment.

steps.text: A team distributes a signed software release.
The publisher uses its private signing key.
Recipients verify using the corresponding public key.
Verification supports origin and integrity. It does not prove the software is harmless.

bank.q: What is the encrypted representation of readable information called?
bank.why: Ciphertext is the encrypted representation.

bank.q: Which key arrangement describes symmetric encryption?
c: A shared secret key for encryption and decryption
A public key alone for every operation
An audit log instead of a key
bank.why: Symmetric encryption relies on a shared secret.

bank.q: Which key does a publisher protect when producing digital signatures?
bank.why: The private signing key must remain under the signer's control.

bank.q: Which key verifies a digital signature made with a private signing key?
bank.why: Verification uses the public key paired with the signing key.

bank.q: A message has a valid signature but is sent in readable form. What is not provided by the signature alone?
bank.why: A signature does not itself conceal the message.

bank.q: Does a valid software signature alone prove the software has no malicious behavior?
c: No, it supports origin and integrity, not harmlessness
Yes, every signed file is safe
Yes, if the file is large
Yes, without checking trust in the signing key
bank.why: A signature is not a behavioral security assessment.

topics.name: Phishing and account defenses
notes: Phishing tries to obtain information or cause a harmful action.
Urgency and attractive offers can be warning signs.
Unique passwords reduce the harm of password reuse.
MFA adds a protection beyond a password.
Updates repair security flaws; reporting suspicious messages helps others respond.
gloss: Deceptive messaging used to induce harmful action
An additional authentication protection beyond a password
Software for creating and storing passwords
Software change that repairs a security flaw

lessons.t: Recognize the request
idea: Judge what the message asks you to do.
Avoid interacting with a suspected phishing message.
recipe: Identify the relevant facts.
Apply the principle in the cited source.
Explain the decision and check its limits.
oops: Treating urgent language as proof the request is legitimate.

steps.text: A message says your account will close unless you sign in immediately.
The request combines urgency with an action involving credentials.
Do not use its link or attachment. Follow your organization's reporting process.
A familiar display name does not make the request trustworthy.

lessons.t: Build layers around accounts
idea: Use distinct passwords and MFA.
Software maintenance remains important.
recipe: Identify the relevant facts.
Apply the principle in the cited source.
Explain the decision and check its limits.
oops: Assuming MFA makes all messages safe.

steps.text: A reused password can expose several accounts if it becomes known.
Use a password manager to support unique account passwords.
Enable MFA where available.
Keep software updated; one protection does not replace the others.

bank.q: A message threatens immediate account closure unless you open its sign-in link. Which warning sign stands out?
c: A verified request through an established workflow
bank.why: Urgency can push a recipient into acting without checking.

bank.q: What is a suitable response to a suspected phishing message?
c: Report it through the established process without engaging
Reply to ask whether it is genuine
Forward its live link to every colleague
bank.why: Reporting supports response without following the suspicious request.

bank.q: A message promises an implausibly large prize in return for account details. What should you recognize?
bank.why: Unrealistic offers can be used to lure recipients.

bank.q: Why use a different password for each account?
c: A disclosed password is less likely to unlock other accounts
It removes the need for MFA
bank.why: Unique passwords reduce exposure from reuse.

bank.q: Which tool can help create and store unique passwords?
bank.why: Password managers support generating and storing distinct passwords.

bank.q: What does MFA add to a password-based sign-in?
bank.why: MFA strengthens sign-in but is not a universal guarantee.

bank.q: Why do security updates matter?
c: They can repair exploitable software flaws
They certify every installed file as harmless
They prove a message came from a colleague
bank.why: Updates address defects in software.

bank.q: A team enables MFA but leaves vulnerable software unpatched. What remains necessary?
c: Share the MFA codes with the team
Treat the system as fully protected
bank.why: Authentication and software maintenance address different weaknesses.

topics.name: Backups and recovery preparation
notes: Maintain offline, encrypted backups.
Ransomware can attack accessible backups as well as live files.
Test backups regularly rather than trusting a job status alone.
Maintain and exercise incident-response and communications plans.
Restoring files does not undo an earlier disclosure of stolen information.
gloss: Copy disconnected from ordinary online access
Exercise that checks whether backup data can be recovered
Prepared approach to restoring needed operations
Planned coordination and notifications during an incident

lessons.t: Protect the recovery copy
idea: An accessible backup can be another ransomware target.
A second copy needs appropriate protection.
recipe: Identify the relevant facts.
Apply the principle in the cited source.
Explain the decision and check its limits.
oops: Treating any second copy as isolated from an attack.

steps.text: An organization copies files to an always-connected shared drive.
Malware with access to that drive could damage the copy too.
Use offline encrypted copies as part of the backup strategy.
Protect the recovery process and validate it with regular testing.

lessons.t: Test the plan
idea: A successful backup job is not a completed recovery exercise.
People and communications are part of preparation.
recipe: Identify the relevant facts.
Apply the principle in the cited source.
Explain the decision and check its limits.
oops: Assuming restored availability cancels a confidentiality breach.

steps.text: A team needs to restore a critical dataset.
Use a controlled exercise to test recoverability.
Review response roles and communications as well as the data.
Use lessons from the exercise to improve the plan.

bank.q: Why does CISA recommend keeping backups offline?
c: Accessible backups may also be encrypted or deleted by ransomware
Offline copies remove the need for all other controls
Offline copies guarantee no data can be stolen
bank.why: Ransomware may target reachable recovery copies.

bank.q: A backup job reports success. What additional preparation is still needed?
bank.why: A job status alone does not demonstrate successful restoration.

bank.q: Which combination matches the cited CISA backup recommendation?
c: Offline encrypted backups with regular tests
Only a screenshot of the file list
Only copies stored on the same affected disk
bank.why: The recommendation combines isolation, encryption and testing.

bank.q: What should accompany technical recovery preparation?
c: An exercised incident-response and communications plan
An untested contact list with no assigned roles
A promise to decide everything during the incident
A policy of avoiding every notification
bank.why: CISA calls for maintained and exercised response and communications planning.

bank.q: A backup is stored on a writable share reachable by compromised systems. What concern remains?
c: The backup could be attacked as well
It is automatically equivalent to an offline copy
Its location proves restoration has been tested
Encryption of the source makes it invulnerable
bank.why: Reachability can expose backup data to the same incident.

bank.q: Files are restored after ransomware, but confidential information had already been stolen. What remains true?
c: Restoration does not reverse the earlier disclosure
The incident no longer requires review
bank.why: Availability recovery and confidentiality impact are different concerns.

bank.q: Which activity best checks whether backup data is usable for recovery?
bank.why: A restore exercise evaluates actual recoverability.

bank.q: Why exercise the communications plan before an incident?
c: To practice coordination and identify weaknesses
To guarantee no incident can occur
bank.why: Exercises prepare people and reveal planning gaps.

topics.name: Governance: roles and policy
notes: Leadership retains responsibility and accountability for cybersecurity risk.
Roles and authority should be defined, communicated and understood.
Policy needs communication and enforcement as well as a written document.
Review policy when requirements, technology, threats or organizational needs change.
NIST CSF is an outcome framework, not a certification checklist or a prescribed implementation method.
gloss: Direction and oversight of cybersecurity risk

lessons.t: Find the owner and authority
idea: An important decision needs a clear responsible role.
Security is an organizational responsibility.
recipe: Identify the relevant facts.
Apply the principle in the cited source.
Explain the decision and check its limits.
oops: Assuming cybersecurity accountability belongs only to a help desk.

steps.text: A team cannot decide who may accept a significant security risk.
Identify the responsible role and the authority assigned to it.
Communicate the decision path to affected staff.
Provide resources appropriate to the responsibilities.

lessons.t: Make policy operational
idea: A policy that no one understands is difficult to apply.
Changing conditions require review.

bank.q: A company has no clear owner for cybersecurity-risk decisions. Which governance improvement is most relevant?

Buy a second monitor for every employee

c: Review and update the policy through the established process
Assume old controls cover every new system
Hide the change from responsible staff

c: Resources are not aligned with assigned responsibilities
The policy font is too small
The organization no longer needs oversight
bank.why: NIST calls for resources commensurate with strategy, roles and policy.

bank.q: What does the NIST CSF 2.0 provide?

A guarantee that no incident will occur

So every employee can authorize every change

Only the age of a logo

To guarantee every packet is harmless

Ignore it if a supplier hosts it

Only counting devices on purchase day

It eliminates the need for review

topics.name: Choosing controls by purpose
notes: Describe a control by both how it is implemented and what it is intended to accomplish. A technical mechanism, management decision, operational activity or physical barrier can support the same security goal.
Preventive controls aim to stop an unwanted action. Detective controls reveal activity. Corrective controls support repair after a problem. A control can serve more than one purpose.

A directive states required behavior; a deterrent discourages violations. A compensating control provides an alternative protection when the primary control cannot be used, subject to approval and validation.

A protection intended to reveal activity or an unwanted event
A protection supporting repair after a problem

The whole organization is now secure

They are always public by design

bank.q: Which boundary rule best matches least necessary access?
c: Allow the documented application path and deny unnecessary paths
Allow all traffic because one service is needed
Use a subnet name as enforcement

topics.name: Applying and validating secure baselines
notes: A secure baseline describes an approved configuration for a defined system role. Adapt it to business requirements rather than treating every device as identical.
Remove unnecessary functions, restrict administrative paths and maintain supported software. Keep the approved configuration and ownership documented.
Configuration drift occurs when the running system departs from the approved state. Review deviations, distinguish authorized changes and correct unsafe ones through change control.

Limiting enabled capabilities to what the system needs

bank.q: What is a secure baseline?
c: An approved configuration for a defined role
A promise that no attacks can occur
A list of unrelated product prices

c: Departure of the running configuration from the approved state
A change in screen brightness only

Apply it everywhere without impact review

bank.why: Least functionality limits the system to required capabilities.

bank.q: What verifies a hardening change?

topics.name: Prioritizing remediation and verifying closure
notes: Vulnerability management includes finding, validating, prioritizing, addressing and tracking weaknesses. A report without an owner and follow-up is not a completed remediation process.
Prioritization considers exposure, exploitation evidence, business impact and available protections alongside technical severity. A number alone does not capture the whole organizational risk.
After remediation, verify the deployed state and rescan or otherwise validate appropriately. If remediation is deferred, document the accountable decision and remaining risk.
gloss: An action that addresses an identified weakness
An assessment of the technical seriousness of a weakness
Ordering responses using exposure, impact and other relevant context
Recorded validation that the selected corrective work resolved a finding

topics.name: Assessing and responding to risk
notes: Risk assessment considers plausible threats, weaknesses, likelihood and consequence in a stated context. Document assumptions because estimates are uncertain and change as the environment changes.

Responses may reduce exposure, avoid the risky activity, share or transfer some consequences, or accept remaining risk through an accountable decision. Buying insurance does not remove every operational impact.

For a simplified quantitative exercise, single loss expectancy equals asset value times exposure factor, and annualized loss expectancy equals that result times annual rate of occurrence. These estimates are planning inputs, not guarantees.
gloss: An estimated loss for one occurrence in a stated model
An estimated annual loss for a risk under stated assumptions
Risk remaining after selected responses or controls
An accountable decision to retain a stated risk

Yes, if the event lasts less than an hour

Only the client who booked it

Ignore the limitation because the category number is high
Proceed only when the battery is new

Only weather at the next flight

Only until the next battery charge
Forever in every case regardless of replacement work

bank.why: Section 107.140(c)(4)(ii) identifies the continuing-status records.

Only if the aircraft exceeds 55 pounds
Only if the work is paid

Only one driver chosen at random
Only people who leave their vehicles

Yes, if the car is newer than the drone

bank.why: The person and property criteria are alternatives.

Ignore the event because there was no injury

Schedule the hardest work in peak heat without breaks
Remove all rest stops to finish sooner
Assume cloud cover removes every heat risk

Depend entirely on finding an unknown stream
Leave water behind to save weight
Assume inactive people never need water

A normal sign that always resolves without help

Ignore the timing of the activity

topics.name: Texas school buses and separate roadways
notes: Stop before a loading or unloading school bus operating its required warning signal, unless a statutory exception applies.
Opposite-direction traffic may be exempt on a separate roadway. A center left-turn lane alone does not create separate roadways.
Movement may resume when the bus moves, its driver signals you to proceed, or its warning signal is no longer operating.
gloss: Roadways divided by a qualifying space or barrier
A left-turn lane, not a separate-roadway barrier
Signal requiring the approaching driver to stop
Travel toward the front of the stopped bus

lessons.t: A turn lane is not a barrier
idea: Road width alone does not establish the exception.
recipe: Read the signal and road layout.
Identify who must wait.
Apply the cited state rule before moving.
oops: Treating a painted turn lane as a physical divider.

steps.text: Scenario: a stopped loading school bus displays its warning signal on the opposite side of a road.
The only divider is a center left-turn lane. Section 545.066(f) says this is not separate roadways.
Stop before reaching the bus. Do not use the opposite-direction exception.

lessons.t: Check the exception, then the release
idea: The exception depends on the roadway occupied by the bus.
recipe: Read the signal and road layout.
Identify who must wait.
Apply the cited state rule before moving.
oops: Assuming a driver behind the bus shares an opposing-roadway exemption.

steps.text: Scenario: a physical barrier separates your roadway from the opposite-direction bus.
The different-roadway exception can apply; it does not exempt traffic following the bus on its own roadway.
If you must stop, wait until one statutory release condition occurs before proceeding.

bank.q: Texas: a loading school bus has its required warning signal operating on a two-lane undivided road. You approach from the opposite direction. What applies?
c: Pass if no child has entered your lane
Stop only if following the bus
Continue because only one lane travels each way
bank.why: Section 545.066(a) covers approaching from either direction.

bank.q: Texas: a center left-turn lane is the only separation between you and an opposing stopped school bus displaying its warning signal. Does that lane establish the separate-roadway exception?
c: Yes, if the turn lane is painted yellow
Yes, if traffic has two lanes each way
Yes, if you remain in the outer lane
bank.why: Section 545.066(f)(2) specifically excludes a left-turn lane alone.

bank.q: Texas: a concrete barrier separates your roadway from an opposing stopped school bus. Which rule is relevant?
c: A bus on a different roadway does not require your stop under this section
Every vehicle in sight must stop regardless of roadway
Only the fastest lane is exempt
The exception requires the bus driver to wave at every opposing car
bank.why: Section 545.066(b)(1) addresses a bus on a different roadway.

bank.q: Texas: you follow a loading school bus on its roadway while its warning signal operates. A barrier separates opposing traffic. What must you do?
c: Stop; the barrier does not exempt traffic behind the bus
Continue because the highway is divided
Pass only on the bus left side
Continue if the opposing roadway is clear
bank.why: You occupy the same roadway as the bus, so the different-roadway exception does not apply.

bank.q: Texas: you stopped for a school bus and its driver now signals you to proceed. Which listed release condition is met?
c: The bus driver has signaled permission to proceed
The bus has necessarily stopped loading permanently
All nearby traffic has acquired priority
The road has become a separate roadway
bank.why: Section 545.066(a)(2)(B) lists the driver signal as a release condition.

bank.q: Texas: which event is a statutory release condition after a required school-bus stop?
c: The car behind you sounds its horn
An adult passenger gestures from your car
You have waited a fixed ten seconds
bank.why: Section 545.066(a)(2)(A) lists the bus resuming motion.

bank.q: Texas: what does a wide road with only painted lane separation change about a school-bus stop?
c: Width alone creates no separate-roadway exception
Four lanes automatically exempt opposing traffic
A wide center lane always exempts traffic
Only vehicles in the nearest lane must stop
bank.why: Section 545.066(f) requires a qualifying separation, not merely more lanes.

bank.q: Texas: you remain stopped while a school bus is stationary and its driver has not signaled you. Which other listed event can end the stop requirement?
c: The required visual warning signal is no longer operating
The children have left your field of view
bank.why: Section 545.066(a)(2)(C) lists the warning signal ending.

topics.name: Florida steady and flashing traffic signals
notes: A permitted right turn on red follows a full stop and yielding; posted prohibitions apply.
A qualifying one-way-to-one-way left turn on red also requires stopping and yielding.
Flashing red follows stop-sign rules; flashing yellow requires caution. Section 316.076 does not cover railroad crossings.
gloss: Pedestrian crossing area with applicable yielding duties

lessons.t: Stop before deciding to turn
idea: A red-turn exception is conditional.
recipe: Read the signal and road layout.
Identify who must wait.
Apply the cited state rule before moving.
oops: Treating an absent prohibition as permission to skip stopping.

steps.text: Scenario: a right turn on red is not prohibited, but pedestrians are crossing.
Stop at the marked line; yield to pedestrians and traffic proceeding under the signal.
Wait until the turn can be made without conflicting with those users.

lessons.t: Do not swap flashing colors
idea: A flashing road signal has a different response from a steady signal.
recipe: Read the signal and road layout.
Identify who must wait.
Apply the cited state rule before moving.
oops: Applying this ordinary-signal lesson to railroad warning lights.

steps.text: Scenario: an ordinary intersection signal flashes red.
Stop at the marked line, or use the statutory crosswalk/view-position fallback if no line exists. Proceed under stop-sign rules.
A flashing yellow instead permits cautious movement. Railroad-crossing rules are separate.

bank.q: Florida: at an ordinary intersection with a flashing red signal, what must a driver do?
c: Stop and apply the rules for proceeding after a stop sign
Wait for the flashing red to become green in every case
Continue if no pedestrian is present
bank.why: Section 316.076(1)(a) requires a stop, then stop-sign rules.

bank.q: Florida: an ordinary traffic signal flashes yellow. Which response applies?
c: Make a mandatory full stop in every case
Treat the signal as an unconditional green arrow
Enter without yielding to any conflict
bank.why: Section 316.076(1)(b) allows movement only with caution.

bank.q: Florida: a right turn on a steady red is otherwise permitted, but a pedestrian has the permitted crossing signal. What applies?
c: Stop and yield before any permitted turn
Turn because vehicles always take priority on red
Yield only if the pedestrian waves
Turn first if you reached the stop line first
bank.why: Section 316.075(1)(c) preserves pedestrian and traffic priority.

bank.q: Florida: a visible No Turn on Red sign applies at your intersection. What does stopping accomplish?
c: It satisfies the stop duty but does not authorize the prohibited turn
It permits a turn after a second stop
It permits the turn whenever no vehicles approach
bank.why: A posted prohibition prevents the red-light turn.

bank.q: Florida: you are on a one-way street meeting another one-way street carrying traffic to the left. When can the left-turn-on-red exception apply?
c: After stopping and yielding, if the turn is not prohibited
After slowing, without a full stop
Only after entering the intersection on red
Whenever the destination street has two lanes
bank.why: Section 316.075(1)(c) describes this one-way-street exception.

bank.q: Florida: a circular green light appears while another vehicle is lawfully within the intersection. What applies?
c: Yield to the vehicle already lawfully there
Proceed because the new green cancels all conflicts
Yield only if the vehicle is an emergency vehicle
Enter first and require the other vehicle to brake
bank.why: Section 316.075(1)(a) retains the yielding requirement.

bank.q: Florida: a clearly marked stop line is present at a flashing red ordinary intersection signal. Where is the required stop?
c: Inside the crosswalk after checking both sides
At the middle of the intersecting road
bank.why: Section 316.076(1)(a) gives the marked line first priority.

bank.q: Florida: can the ordinary flashing-signal rule in section 316.076 be used as the full rule for a railroad-highway crossing?
c: No; the section expressly excludes those crossings
Yes; every flashing light has identical rules
Yes, if the train is not yet visible
bank.why: Section 316.076(2) directs railroad crossings to separate provisions.

topics.name: Florida school buses and median exceptions
notes: Stop for a stopped school bus displaying its stop signal and do not pass until that signal is withdrawn.
The opposing-direction exception requires an unpaved space at least five feet wide, a raised median, or a physical barrier.
An ordinary paved center turn lane does not satisfy that exception; following traffic must still stop.
gloss: Nonpaved separation; five-foot minimum for this exception
Elevated divider listed separately in the statute
A physical divider between opposing traffic
Bus signal that must be withdrawn before passing

lessons.t: Test the actual divider
idea: The five-foot condition applies to unpaved space.
recipe: Read the signal and road layout.
Identify who must wait.
Apply the cited state rule before moving.
oops: Treating any narrow strip of grass as sufficient.

steps.text: Scenario: you approach an opposing school bus across an unpaved divider four feet wide, with no raised median or barrier.
That divider fails the at-least-five-foot unpaved-space condition.
Stop for the displayed bus stop signal. A five-foot unpaved space would meet that specific divider condition.

lessons.t: The exception belongs to opposing traffic
idea: A divided highway does not exempt everyone.
recipe: Read the signal and road layout.
Identify who must wait.
Apply the cited state rule before moving.
oops: Using an opposing-direction exception while following the bus.

steps.text: Scenario: a raised median separates the two directions.
An opposing driver can qualify for the exception; a driver behind the bus cannot use it.
Following traffic stops for the bus stop signal and must not pass until it is withdrawn.

bank.q: Florida: a stopped school bus displays its stop signal on an undivided two-way road. You approach from the opposite direction. What must you do?
c: Continue if the bus doors face away from you
Stop only if children have reached your lane
Continue if two cars ahead have passed
bank.why: Section 316.172 requires a full stop unless its divided-highway exception applies.

bank.q: Florida: you are behind a stopped school bus displaying its stop signal on a divided highway. Does the opposing-direction exception cover you?
c: Yes, whenever the highway has a median
Yes, if you can pass in another lane
Yes, when the speed limit is high
bank.why: Section 316.172(2) exempts qualifying opposing traffic, not following traffic.

bank.q: Florida: opposing traffic is separated from a stopped school bus by an unpaved space exactly five feet wide. With no other conflict, which bus-stop rule applies to that opposing driver?
c: The statutory divider exception can apply
The unpaved space must be more than five feet
The exception applies only at six feet
The exception requires a painted center turn lane as well
bank.why: At least five feet includes exactly five feet.

bank.q: Florida: an opposing school bus has its stop signal displayed. Only four feet of unpaved space separates directions, with no raised median or barrier. What applies?
c: Stop; this unpaved space is too narrow for the exception
Continue because any grass divider is enough
Continue because opposing traffic is always exempt
Stop only if the bus driver gestures
bank.why: The unpaved-space alternative requires at least five feet.

bank.q: Florida: which divider is separately listed as qualifying for the opposing-direction school-bus exception?
c: An ordinary painted center turn lane
A wide paved shoulder on your side
bank.why: Section 316.172(2) lists raised medians separately from the five-foot unpaved-space alternative.

bank.q: Florida: a paved road has several lanes in each direction and only an ordinary painted center turn lane between them. An opposing school bus displays its stop signal. What applies?
c: Stop; the described divider does not meet the statutory exception
Continue because the road has multiple lanes
Continue if you use the farthest lane
Stop only if another driver has stopped
bank.why: The exception requires a qualifying unpaved space, raised median or physical barrier.

bank.q: Florida: while you wait behind a stopped school bus, its stop signal remains displayed and a passenger says all children are seated. May you pass on that basis?
c: No; wait until the stop signal is withdrawn
Yes, because a passenger can release traffic
Yes, after checking the bus windows
Yes, if the bus has no visible pedestrians beside it
bank.why: Section 316.172(1)(a) prohibits passing until the stop signal is withdrawn.

bank.q: Florida: a physical barrier separates your opposite-direction roadway from a stopped school bus. Which statement matches the exception?
c: Opposing traffic is not required to stop under this bus provision
Every vehicle on both roadways must stop
Only drivers behind the bus are exempt
The physical barrier must also be an unpaved space
bank.why: A physical barrier is one of the separate alternatives in section 316.172(2).

topics.name: Alabama roundabout decisions
notes: Enter to the right of the central island and circulate counterclockwise.
Yield to circulating traffic and to pedestrians and bicyclists at crossings; enter only with a safe gap.
If you miss an exit, go around again. Cars should not use the truck apron.
If an emergency vehicle approaches while you are inside, continue to your exit, then pull over.
gloss: Vehicles already traveling around the island
Space sufficient for a safe entrance
Inside paved area for large-vehicle rear wheels
Pedestrian or bicycle crossing near the departure road

lessons.t: Enter and exit without forcing a conflict
idea: A roundabout entry is a yielding decision.
recipe: Identify the conditions and conflicts.
Apply the rule or safety principle in the cited section.
Explain what to do and what could change the decision.
oops: Entering just because a circulating driver appears to be slowing.

steps.text: Scenario: a car is circulating from your left while a person is crossing the entry.
Slow down and yield to both conflicts; wait for a safe gap.
Enter to the right of the island, keep speed low and yield at the exit crossing.

lessons.t: Missed exits and emergency vehicles
idea: Continue around rather than reversing or cutting across.
recipe: Identify the conditions and conflicts.
Apply the rule or safety principle in the cited section.
Explain what to do and what could change the decision.
oops: Backing up inside a roundabout or stopping there to let an emergency vehicle pass.

steps.text: Scenario: you miss the intended exit. Continue around to reach it on the next circuit.
If an emergency vehicle approaches while you are inside, continue to your exit before pulling over.
Leave the truck apron for the large vehicles it is designed to accommodate.

bank.q: Alabama: a vehicle is already circulating from your left as you approach a roundabout. What is your entry decision?
c: Yield and wait for a safe gap
Enter because arriving traffic has priority
Stop the circulating vehicle with a horn
Enter ahead of it if you plan the first exit
bank.why: The roundabout section assigns priority to traffic already circulating.

bank.q: Alabama: how do you enter and circulate around the central island?
c: Enter to its right and travel counterclockwise
Enter to its left and travel clockwise
Choose either direction if no car is present
Use the apron to travel straight across
bank.why: The manual describes one-way counterclockwise circulation.

bank.q: Alabama: you pass your intended roundabout exit. What should you do?
c: Continue around again to that exit
Stop and cross the central island
bank.why: The manual directs another circuit and prohibits backing up.

bank.q: Alabama: an emergency vehicle approaches after you have entered the roundabout. What does the manual recommend?
c: Continue to your exit, then pull over
Stop immediately in the circulating lane
Drive onto the truck apron and wait there
bank.why: The manual distinguishes the response inside from the response before entry.

bank.q: Alabama: what is the intended purpose of a roundabout truck apron?
c: Room for the rear wheels of large turning vehicles
A shortcut for cars taking the first exit
A parking area for broken-down SUVs
An extra passing lane for pickup trucks
bank.why: The apron accommodates large-vehicle off-tracking, not ordinary car travel.

bank.q: Alabama: a bicyclist is crossing at your roundabout exit. What applies?
c: Yield to the bicyclist before exiting
Exit first because circulating vehicles always outrank crossings
Yield only at the entry, never the exit
Honk to transfer priority to your vehicle
bank.why: The manual includes yielding to pedestrians and bicycles while exiting.

bank.q: Alabama: should you normally stop inside a roundabout when your exit is still ahead?
c: No; keep moving unless stopping is necessary to avoid danger
Yes; stop at every entry you pass
Yes; wait inside until no other vehicles remain
No; stopping is forbidden even to avoid a collision
bank.why: Avoid unnecessary stops, while retaining the need to stop to avoid danger.

bank.q: Alabama: while approaching a roundabout, which combination is appropriate?
c: Slow down, obey signs and check entry conflicts
Maintain the approach-road speed and select a gap later
Yield only to vehicles larger than yours
Accelerate to discourage traffic from entering
bank.why: The entry sequence begins with reducing speed and observing signs and conflicts.

topics.name: Alabama right-of-way conflicts

refs.section: Right of Way and Yielding, printed pp. 62-63

notes: At simultaneous uncontrolled entries from different roads, the driver on the left yields to the driver on the right.
A left turn yields to an oncoming vehicle in the intersection or close enough to be an immediate hazard.
Stop and yield before entering a public road from a private road or driveway.
For an approaching emergency vehicle using warning lights and siren, clear an intersection before pulling aside and stopping.
gloss: Intersection without controlling signs or signals
Traffic too close for the planned movement to be safe
Access that yields when joining a public road
Allow the conflicting road user to proceed

lessons.t: Arrival time and movement both matter
idea: The right-side rule does not replace every other yielding duty.
recipe: Identify the conditions and conflicts.
Apply the rule or safety principle in the cited section.
Explain what to do and what could change the decision.
oops: Using the simultaneous-entry rule to justify an unsafe left turn.

steps.text: Scenario: two vehicles enter an uncontrolled intersection from different roads at about the same time.
The driver on the left yields to the driver on the right.
In a separate left-turn scenario, yield to conflicting oncoming traffic that is in or too close to the intersection.

refs.section: Right of Way and Yielding, printed pp. 62-63

lessons.t: Enter from a driveway and respond to emergency traffic
idea: Your access road and position affect the action.
recipe: Identify the conditions and conflicts.
Apply the rule or safety principle in the cited section.
Explain what to do and what could change the decision.
oops: Stopping inside an intersection and obstructing the emergency route.

steps.text: Scenario: you are leaving a private driveway for a public street. Stop and yield to public-road traffic.
If an emergency vehicle approaches with lights and siren while you are in an intersection, clear the intersection first.
Then pull to the side and stop; wait until the emergency vehicle has passed.

refs.section: Right of Way and Yielding, printed pp. 62-63

bank.q: Alabama: two vehicles enter an uncontrolled intersection from different roads at about the same time. You are to the left. What applies?
c: Yield to the vehicle on your right
Proceed because your road looks wider
Proceed because uncontrolled means no yielding rule
Yield only if the other vehicle is a truck
bank.why: The manual gives the simultaneous-entry rule in its right-of-way section.

refs.section: Right of Way and Yielding, printed pp. 62-63

bank.q: Alabama: an oncoming vehicle is close enough to be an immediate hazard as you prepare to turn left. What applies?
c: Turn first if you have signaled
Turn first if your car is partly over the centerline
Require the oncoming driver to stop
bank.why: A left turn must yield to the described opposing conflict.

refs.section: Right of Way and Yielding, printed pp. 62-63

bank.q: Alabama: you leave a private driveway to enter a public road. Which action fits the manual?
c: Stop and yield to public-road traffic
Merge without stopping if your driveway is paved
Yield only to vehicles coming from the right
Signal and rely on public-road drivers to make space
bank.why: The manual requires stopping and yielding from private access.

refs.section: Right of Way and Yielding, printed pp. 62-63

bank.q: Alabama: an emergency vehicle uses flashing warning lights and a siren while you are inside an intersection. What is the appropriate sequence?
c: Clear the intersection, then pull aside and stop
Continue at your original speed until your destination
Make an abrupt U-turn in the intersection
bank.why: The right-of-way section directs clearing the intersection before stopping.

refs.section: Right of Way and Yielding, printed pp. 62-63

bank.q: Alabama: a green arrow permits your turn, but another vehicle is lawfully using the intersection. What remains necessary?
c: Proceed because the arrow removes every yielding duty
Yield only if the other vehicle also has an arrow
bank.why: The manual preserves yielding duties for traffic lawfully in the intersection.

refs.section: Right of Way and Yielding, printed pp. 62-63

bank.q: Alabama: at a yield sign, pedestrians are legally crossing the road you intend to enter. What applies?
c: Slow down and stop if needed to yield
Proceed as long as you do not accelerate
Treat the sign as applying only to motor vehicles
Wait only if a pedestrian signals to you
bank.why: A yield-controlled entry includes legally crossing pedestrians.

refs.section: Right of Way and Yielding, printed pp. 62-63

bank.q: Alabama: your vehicle enters an uncontrolled intersection at an unlawful speed. What does the manual say about a right-of-way you otherwise might have had?
c: Speed has no effect on that rule
You gain priority because stopping is harder
Only vehicles on your left must accommodate you
bank.why: The manual expressly says unlawful entry speed forfeits that right-of-way.

refs.section: Right of Way and Yielding, printed pp. 62-63

bank.q: Alabama: after pulling aside and stopping for an approaching emergency vehicle with lights and siren, when should you proceed?
c: After the emergency vehicle has passed and the way is safe
As soon as the siren seems quieter
When another waiting driver starts to move
bank.why: The manual says not to proceed until the emergency vehicle has passed.

refs.section: Right of Way and Yielding, printed pp. 62-63

topics.name: Alaska uncontrolled intersections
notes: Reduce speed and keep the vehicle under control at an uncontrolled intersection.
If two approaching vehicles would conflict, the driver on the left yields to the driver on the right.
Approaching from the right does not excuse excessive speed or remove the need to check for vehicles already inside.
gloss: Road without stop signs, yield signs or traffic lights controlling the intersection
Speed and attention allowing a safe response
An intersection already containing a road user

lessons.t: Being on the right is not a reason to rush
idea: The approach-speed duty and yielding rule work together.
recipe: Identify the conditions and conflicts.
Apply the rule or safety principle in the cited section.
Explain what to do and what could change the decision.
oops: Assuming right-side approach guarantees that everyone else will stop.

steps.text: Scenario: two vehicles approach an uncontrolled intersection at a conflicting time; you are on the right.
Slow down and retain control rather than assuming the other driver will yield.
Check for a vehicle already inside before deciding the route is clear.

lessons.t: Identify the left-side yielding duty
idea: Look at the relative positions and collision risk.
recipe: Identify the conditions and conflicts.
Apply the rule or safety principle in the cited section.
Explain what to do and what could change the decision.
oops: Using the size of the vehicle or width of the street as the priority rule.

steps.text: Scenario: another vehicle approaches from your right at a time that would create a collision.
You are the driver on the left, so yield.
Proceed only after the conflict clears; keep checking the intersection and its crossing users.

bank.q: Alaska: two vehicles approach an uncontrolled intersection at a conflicting time, and you are on the left. What must you do?
c: Yield to the vehicle on your right
Proceed if your street has more pavement
Proceed if your vehicle is larger
Rely on the other driver to choose a direction
bank.why: The intersections section assigns the yielding duty to the driver on the left.

bank.q: Alaska: you approach an uncontrolled intersection from the right. Does that remove your duty to slow down?
c: No; slow down and retain control
Yes; the other driver must handle the entire conflict
Yes, if your vehicle has good brakes
Only if there are pedestrians visible
bank.why: The manual explicitly retains the slowing and control duties.

bank.q: Alaska: you are approaching from the right, but another vehicle is already within the uncontrolled intersection. What should guide your decision?
c: Account for the vehicle already inside rather than assuming priority
Use your right-side position to enter immediately
Require that vehicle to reverse out
Enter if the other car is smaller
bank.why: The manual qualifies the right-side rule when another vehicle is already within the intersection.

bank.q: Alaska: which intersection fits this lesson on an uncontrolled route?
c: One without controlling stop signs, yield signs or traffic lights
Every intersection where your own light is green
An intersection with a posted stop sign facing you
An intersection where an officer is actively directing traffic
bank.why: The manual defines the unprotected route by the absence of those controls.

bank.q: Alaska: why is relying entirely on the other driver to yield unsafe at an uncontrolled intersection?
c: Right-of-way cannot be treated as a guarantee that the other driver will give way
It is always the largest vehicle that proceeds first
The driver on the left is never subject to a yielding duty
All uncontrolled intersections require a traffic officer
bank.why: The manual warns the right-side driver against assuming the right-of-way will be given.

bank.q: Alaska: as you approach a crossroad on an unprotected route, which preparation is required?
c: Reduce to a reasonable speed and keep the vehicle under control
Accelerate so your time in the intersection is shorter
Keep a fixed highway speed regardless of conditions
Look only toward traffic on your right
bank.why: The approach rule covers both speed and control.

bank.q: Alaska: two cars would collide if both continued through an uncontrolled intersection. Which fact determines the left-side yielding duty described here?
c: Which driver sounds a horn first
bank.why: The stated yielding rule concerns the vehicle on the left and the vehicle on the right.

bank.q: Alaska: after the vehicle on your right clears an uncontrolled intersection, what is the sensible next step?
c: Check the remaining conflicts before proceeding
Enter without another look because the rule has been satisfied once
Assume every pedestrian has also crossed
Increase speed before checking the cross street
bank.why: Yielding to one conflict does not establish that the entire intersection is clear.

topics.name: Alaska lighting requirements and visibility

refs.section: Night Driving and Use of Lighting Equipment, printed pp. 54-55

notes: The manual requires headlights from half an hour after sunset to half an hour before sunrise, and in daytime visibility of 1,000 feet or less due to listed weather or airborne conditions.
Dim at least 500 feet from an oncoming vehicle and at least 300 feet behind a vehicle traveling in the same direction.
Use low beams in rain, fog, snow or dust. Parking lights alone are not for a moving vehicle.
gloss: Headlight setting used to limit glare
Gap behind a vehicle going your direction
Distance within which road users and hazards can be seen

lessons.t: Keep the three distances separate
idea: The daytime visibility threshold is not a dimming distance.
recipe: Identify the conditions and conflicts.
Apply the rule or safety principle in the cited section.
Explain what to do and what could change the decision.
oops: Swapping the oncoming and following distances.

steps.text: Scenario: daytime snow limits visibility to 800 feet. Turn on the headlights.
An approaching vehicle requires low beams at 500 feet or more.
A vehicle you follow requires dimming at 300 feet or more.

refs.section: Night Driving and Use of Lighting Equipment, printed pp. 54-55

lessons.t: Choose lighting that helps rather than blinds
idea: Better visibility is not simply the brightest possible lamp.
recipe: Identify the conditions and conflicts.
Apply the rule or safety principle in the cited section.
Explain what to do and what could change the decision.
oops: Assuming parking lamps provide the same moving-vehicle function as headlights.

steps.text: Scenario: fog reduces the view ahead. Use low beams rather than high beams.
Do not substitute parking lights alone while moving.
Keep lights and windshield clean, and avoid staring directly at approaching headlights.

refs.section: Night Driving and Use of Lighting Equipment, printed pp. 54-55

bank.q: Alaska: daytime snowfall reduces visibility to 800 feet. What does the manual require for lighting?
c: Wait until half an hour after sunset
Keep headlights off to reduce glare for others
bank.why: The listed daytime visibility threshold is 1,000 feet or less.

refs.section: Night Driving and Use of Lighting Equipment, printed pp. 54-55

bank.q: Alaska: by what distance must high beams be dimmed for an oncoming vehicle under the manual?
c: Only when the vehicles are side by side
Only after the other driver flashes their lights
bank.why: The oncoming-vehicle dimming distance is 500 feet or more.

refs.section: Night Driving and Use of Lighting Equipment, printed pp. 54-55

bank.q: Alaska: what dimming distance does the manual give when following a vehicle traveling in your direction?
c: Only when the rear window is open
bank.why: The same-direction dimming distance is 300 feet or more.

refs.section: Night Driving and Use of Lighting Equipment, printed pp. 54-55

bank.q: Alaska: which beam setting is recommended for rain, fog, snow or dust?
bank.why: The manual lists low beams for those reduced-visibility conditions.

refs.section: Night Driving and Use of Lighting Equipment, printed pp. 54-55

bank.q: Alaska: which nighttime interval is stated in the manual as requiring headlights?
c: Half an hour after sunset through half an hour before sunrise
Only during a posted winter season

refs.section: Night Driving and Use of Lighting Equipment, printed pp. 54-55

bank.q: Alaska: may a moving vehicle use only its parking lights as a substitute for headlights?

refs.section: Night Driving and Use of Lighting Equipment, printed pp. 54-55

bank.q: Alaska: what should you do when approaching headlights create glare?
c: Avoid staring directly at them and keep monitoring your path
Fix your gaze on the brightest lamp

refs.section: Night Driving and Use of Lighting Equipment, printed pp. 54-55

bank.q: Alaska: daylight smoke reduces visibility to exactly 1,000 feet. Does that meet the listed headlight threshold?

Only if it is also raining

topics.name: Arkansas ordinary signals and turn arrows

refs.section: Lighted Traffic Signals, Flashing Lights, Lighted Arrows and Right on Red, printed pp. 23-25

notes: A steady yellow warns of the change to red; stop if safe and do not start from an already stopped position on yellow.
Flashing red requires a complete stop and safe entry; flashing yellow calls for slowing and caution.
A red arrow prohibits the indicated turn. A flashing yellow arrow permits a left turn only after yielding to oncoming traffic and pedestrians.
For an otherwise permitted right on red, stop fully, check traffic and pedestrians and obey a prohibiting sign.

lessons.t: Do not confuse a flashing arrow with protection
idea: An allowed turn can still require waiting.
recipe: Identify the conditions and conflicts.
Apply the rule or safety principle in the cited section.

steps.text: Scenario: a flashing yellow arrow appears for your left turn and oncoming traffic is close.
Yield to the oncoming traffic and pedestrians; wait for a safe opening.
A steady red arrow instead prohibits that turn.

refs.section: Lighted Traffic Signals, Flashing Lights, Lighted Arrows and Right on Red, printed pp. 23-25

lessons.t: Separate stopping from permission to enter
idea: A stop is required before considering a red-light exception.
recipe: Identify the conditions and conflicts.
Apply the rule or safety principle in the cited section.
Explain what to do and what could change the decision.

steps.text: Scenario: a right turn on red is not prohibited. Stop completely and check both traffic and pedestrians.
At a flashing red ordinary intersection signal, stop and proceed only when safe.
If already stopped when steady yellow appears, do not start into the intersection.

refs.section: Lighted Traffic Signals, Flashing Lights, Lighted Arrows and Right on Red, printed pp. 23-25

bank.q: Arkansas: a flashing yellow arrow controls your left turn and oncoming traffic is approaching. What applies?
c: Yield to oncoming traffic and pedestrians before turning
Turn immediately as a fully protected movement
Wait only for pedestrians, not vehicles
Proceed before opposing traffic can reach its stop line

refs.section: Lighted Traffic Signals, Flashing Lights, Lighted Arrows and Right on Red, printed pp. 23-25

bank.q: Arkansas: a steady red arrow points in the direction you intend to turn. What does it mean?
c: Do not turn in that direction
Turn whenever a pedestrian is absent
Treat it as a flashing yellow arrow

refs.section: Lighted Traffic Signals, Flashing Lights, Lighted Arrows and Right on Red, printed pp. 23-25

bank.q: Arkansas: you approach an ordinary intersection displaying a flashing red signal. What is required?
c: A full stop, then proceed only when safe
Proceed if you are traveling straight
Stop only if another road has a stop sign

refs.section: Lighted Traffic Signals, Flashing Lights, Lighted Arrows and Right on Red, printed pp. 23-25

bank.q: Arkansas: an ordinary traffic signal flashes yellow. Which response fits the guide?
c: Treat it as a protected left-turn arrow
Stop and remain until it turns green in all cases
Maintain speed because traffic must yield to you

refs.section: Lighted Traffic Signals, Flashing Lights, Lighted Arrows and Right on Red, printed pp. 23-25

bank.q: Arkansas: you are already stopped at the intersection when the signal changes to steady yellow. What should you do?
c: Remain stopped rather than starting through
Enter if you can clear the first crosswalk
Start moving if the driver behind honks

refs.section: Lighted Traffic Signals, Flashing Lights, Lighted Arrows and Right on Red, printed pp. 23-25

bank.q: Arkansas: a right turn on red is otherwise allowed. What comes before making it?
c: A complete stop and a check for conflicting traffic and pedestrians
Only a reduction to walking speed
A horn signal and immediate entry
A stop only if there are cars behind you

refs.section: Lighted Traffic Signals, Flashing Lights, Lighted Arrows and Right on Red, printed pp. 23-25

bank.q: Arkansas: what effect does a posted prohibition have on a right turn on red?
c: It applies only if the vehicle is a truck
It disappears after a complete stop
It permits turning after a second stop

bank.q: Arkansas: your signal is green but opposing traffic is lawfully already in the intersection. What should you do?

Drive into the space because your green just began
Require it to stop in the middle
Proceed if your vehicle is smaller
bank.why: The guide requires the existing intersection conflict to clear.

refs.section: Lighted Traffic Signals, Flashing Lights, Lighted Arrows and Right on Red, printed pp. 23-25

topics.name: Arkansas railroad-crossing decisions

refs.section: Railroad Crossing Signs and Emergency Notification Systems, printed pp. 28-29

notes: Cross only when there is space for the whole vehicle beyond the tracks. Never race a train or drive around a lowered gate.
Flashing red railroad lights are not an ordinary intersection flashing-red exception: do not cross while they continue.
The crossbuck marks the crossing and requires yielding to trains. The advance warning sign is round and yellow.
The Emergency Notification System sign identifies the railroad contact and the particular crossing for an emergency report.
gloss: Railroad emergency contact and crossing identification
Enough room to put the entire vehicle beyond the tracks

lessons.t: A green road ahead is not enough clearance
idea: Check the far side before committing to the crossing.
recipe: Identify the conditions and conflicts.
Apply the rule or safety principle in the cited section.
Explain what to do and what could change the decision.
oops: Following another vehicle onto the tracks without an exit space.

steps.text: Scenario: traffic beyond the crossing is backed up onto the space your car would need.
Wait before the tracks until the whole vehicle will fit on the far side.
Do not try to beat a train or go around a gate to avoid waiting.

refs.section: Railroad Crossing Signs and Emergency Notification Systems, printed pp. 28-29

lessons.t: Railroad warnings are a separate case
idea: A complete stop alone does not permit crossing active railroad warnings.
recipe: Identify the conditions and conflicts.
Apply the rule or safety principle in the cited section.
Explain what to do and what could change the decision.
oops: Treating railroad flashing red as permission to stop and then immediately drive through.

steps.text: Scenario: the last visible rail car has passed, but red crossing lights are still flashing.
Stay out of the crossing; a second train or active warning can remain.
For an emergency report, use the crossing identity and railroad contact on the ENS sign.

refs.section: Railroad Crossing Signs and Emergency Notification Systems, printed pp. 28-29

bank.q: Arkansas: traffic beyond railroad tracks leaves insufficient room for your entire car. What should you do?
c: Enter and stop between the rails
Use the shoulder beyond the crossing to store the rear of the car
Follow the car ahead closely so you both fit
bank.why: The guide says not to cross without sufficient room on the opposite side.

refs.section: Railroad Crossing Signs and Emergency Notification Systems, printed pp. 28-29

bank.q: Arkansas: the railroad warning lights continue flashing red, but no train is currently visible. What applies?
c: Do not cross while the warning remains active
Stop briefly, then use the ordinary intersection rule
Cross if you lower a window first
Cross if the gates appear fully open
bank.why: The railroad section specifically says not to cross even if no train appears.

refs.section: Railroad Crossing Signs and Emergency Notification Systems, printed pp. 28-29

bank.q: Arkansas: what does a crossbuck at the tracks require?
c: Yield the right-of-way to a train
Treat the crossing as a passing zone
Stop only if the sign is yellow
Give your vehicle priority after sounding its horn
bank.why: The crossbuck marks the grade crossing and the train yielding duty.

refs.section: Railroad Crossing Signs and Emergency Notification Systems, printed pp. 28-29

bank.q: Arkansas: what is the purpose of the round yellow railroad advance-warning sign?
c: Warn of tracks ahead so you can slow, observe and prepare to stop
Mark the exact place to park on the rails
Identify a road reserved for trains only
bank.why: The guide distinguishes the advance warning from the crossbuck at the tracks.

refs.section: Railroad Crossing Signs and Emergency Notification Systems, printed pp. 28-29

bank.q: Arkansas: can a driver go around a lowered railroad gate if the far lane appears clear?
c: Yes, if only one track is visible
Yes, if no horn is audible
bank.why: The guide prohibits going around crossing gates.

refs.section: Railroad Crossing Signs and Emergency Notification Systems, printed pp. 28-29

bank.q: Arkansas: what information does a railroad Emergency Notification System sign provide?
c: Railroad emergency contact details and a crossing identifier
The time the next passenger train is due
A universal permission to cross when the road is empty
bank.why: The ENS section describes its role in identifying and reporting a crossing emergency.

refs.section: Railroad Crossing Signs and Emergency Notification Systems, printed pp. 28-29

bank.q: Arkansas: why is shifting gears on the tracks discouraged for a manual-transmission vehicle?
c: It can increase the risk of stalling on the crossing
It automatically gives a train a stop signal
It cancels the road warning lights
It changes a crossbuck into a stop sign
bank.why: The guide recommends avoiding a gear change during the crossing to reduce stall risk.

refs.section: Railroad Crossing Signs and Emergency Notification Systems, printed pp. 28-29

bank.q: Arkansas: a train appears far enough away that you think you can race it to the crossing. What does the guide advise?
c: Do not try to beat the train
Accelerate if the gate has not finished lowering
Use the opposing lane for a faster crossing
Proceed if a car ahead also crosses
bank.why: The railroad section explicitly rejects trying to beat an approaching train.

refs.section: Railroad Crossing Signs and Emergency Notification Systems, printed pp. 28-29

topics.name: Colorado mountain-road planning
notes: Use lower gears to help control speed down steep grades.
Do not use an oncoming lane to pass where a hill, curve or other obstruction blocks the view of approaching traffic.
Prepare for changing weather, wildlife, bicyclists, rocks and concealed intersections.
Uphill traffic has priority over downhill traffic. A vehicle struggling uphill should use a safe turnout or the right lane to allow passing.
gloss: Gear supporting speed control on a descent
Visible road available for a decision
Safe place outside the travel path to allow others past

lessons.t: Choose the descent before speed builds
idea: A steep road needs an appropriate speed-control plan.
recipe: Identify the conditions and conflicts.
Apply the rule or safety principle in the cited section.
Explain what to do and what could change the decision.
oops: Relying on the normal level-road driving plan on a steep descent.

steps.text: Scenario: a long downhill mountain grade is ahead. Use a lower gear to help control speed.
Continue scanning for rocks, wildlife and changes in the road.
Avoid treating the posted maximum as a target independent of the conditions.

lessons.t: Do not pass into an unseen conflict
idea: A slow vehicle ahead does not create a visible passing gap.
recipe: Identify the conditions and conflicts.
Apply the rule or safety principle in the cited section.
Explain what to do and what could change the decision.
oops: Using urgency from traffic behind as permission for a blind pass.

steps.text: Scenario: a hill crest blocks the view of the oncoming lane. Do not use that lane to pass.
If your own vehicle struggles uphill, use a safe place to pull off or remain in the right lane.
For opposing traffic on a constrained mountain road, remember the uphill priority described by DMV.

bank.q: Colorado: what does DMV recommend to help control speed on a steep mountain descent?
c: Use a higher gear solely to reduce engine sound
bank.why: The mountain-driving page recommends lower gears for steep downhill speed control.

bank.q: Colorado: a hill crest blocks your view of opposing traffic. May you use the oncoming lane to pass a slow vehicle?
c: Yes, if the slow vehicle has hazard lights
Yes, if there is no car immediately at the crest
bank.why: DMV prohibits an oncoming-lane pass when the available view is obstructed.

bank.q: Colorado: on a mountain road, which opposing vehicle has the right-of-way in the DMV guidance?
c: The vehicle going downhill in every case
The larger vehicle in every case
The vehicle that first sounds its horn
bank.why: The mountain-driving page states the uphill priority.

bank.q: Colorado: your vehicle is struggling to climb a steep roadway. What does DMV recommend to help other traffic pass?
c: Pull off at the first safe place or remain in the right lane
Stop immediately in the travel lane
Drive partly in the oncoming lane
Require every following vehicle to remain behind for the entire climb
bank.why: The guidance describes safe pull-offs or use of the right lane.

bank.q: Colorado: which combination of hazards should you anticipate on mountain roads?
c: Weather changes, rocks, wildlife and bicyclists
Only the hazards present at the start of the drive
Only marked intersections and parked vehicles
bank.why: DMV lists multiple changing mountain-road hazards.

bank.q: Colorado: a curve hides the oncoming lane and the driver behind you is impatient. What controls the passing decision?
c: The obstructed view makes the oncoming-lane pass unsafe and prohibited
The following driver can authorize your pass
The slow vehicle ahead must move into oncoming traffic
A horn signal makes the curve safe to pass
bank.why: The visibility restriction is not removed by pressure from another driver.

bank.q: Colorado: trees and brush hide the next intersection on a mountain road. What should you be prepared for?
c: Unexpected cross traffic at the concealed intersection
Automatic priority because your road is steeper
No intersection unless you see a traffic light
Permission to pass through the opposing lane
bank.why: DMV warns about intersections concealed by vegetation.

bank.q: Colorado: a useful plan for a steep descent is best described as which choice?
c: Select appropriate gearing and keep reassessing road conditions
Select a gear once and stop scanning
Coast freely until a turn appears
Follow the vehicle ahead closely to copy its braking
bank.why: Lower gearing supports control while attention to conditions remains necessary.

topics.name: Colorado winter traction and snowplows

refs.section: Driving in Ice, Snow; Seasonal Driving

notes: Snow and ice reduce grip and lengthen stopping. Bridges, overpasses and shaded areas can remain icy when nearby pavement is clear.
Four-wheel drive does not make a vehicle stop sooner on a slippery surface. Slow down and leave extra following space.
Clear windows completely, and leave extra room for pedestrians and bicyclists avoiding snow.
Do not pass a working city, county or state snowplow with yellow lights flashing when it is traveling in tandem with other plows.
gloss: Gap available to react and stop
Road section that may retain ice longer

lessons.t: Do not let four-wheel drive hide stopping risk
idea: Extra ability to move is not extra ability to stop.
recipe: Identify the conditions and conflicts.
Apply the rule or safety principle in the cited section.
Explain what to do and what could change the decision.
oops: Using normal dry-road following space because all wheels are driven.

steps.text: Scenario: your four-wheel-drive vehicle accelerates easily on snow.
Do not infer that its stopping distance is short; reduce speed and enlarge the following gap.
Treat a shaded bridge as potentially icy even if the road before it appears clear.

refs.section: Driving in Ice, Snow; Seasonal Driving

lessons.t: See clearly and give winter road users room
idea: Winter safety includes visibility and working equipment.
recipe: Identify the conditions and conflicts.
Apply the rule or safety principle in the cited section.
Explain what to do and what could change the decision.
oops: Treating a short trip as a reason to skip clearing the windows.

steps.text: Scenario: only a small patch of windshield has been scraped clear. Remove the remaining ice, snow and frost before traveling.
Give pedestrians and bicyclists room to move around roadside snow.
Stay behind working tandem plows displaying yellow warning lights rather than passing between them.

refs.section: Driving in Ice, Snow; Seasonal Driving

bank.q: Colorado: your four-wheel-drive vehicle accelerates well on snow. What should you conclude about stopping?
c: It does not automatically stop sooner than a conventional car
Its stopping distance is always cut in half
It can safely follow at the dry-road gap
bank.why: The DMV page separates increased driving traction from stopping ability.

refs.section: Driving in Ice, Snow; Seasonal Driving

bank.q: Colorado: which surface may remain icy when nearby road pavement is clear?
c: Only pavement directly under a streetlight
Only a road with visible falling snow
bank.why: The winter page specifically identifies bridges, overpasses and shade.

refs.section: Driving in Ice, Snow; Seasonal Driving

bank.q: Colorado: how should following space change on snow or ice?
c: Reduce it to keep the vehicle ahead visible
Keep the dry-road gap if you have four-wheel drive
Use the same gap but turn on high beams
bank.why: Reduced grip requires more room to stop.

refs.section: Driving in Ice, Snow; Seasonal Driving

bank.q: Colorado: a working state snowplow has yellow lights flashing and is traveling in tandem with another plow. May you pass it?
c: Yes, if a gap briefly opens between the plows
Yes, if your car has winter tires
Yes, if you use the shoulder

refs.section: Driving in Ice, Snow; Seasonal Driving

bank.q: Colorado: before a short winter trip, only a small viewing patch has been scraped in the windshield. What is appropriate?
c: Remove all ice, snow and frost from the windows
Drive slowly and rely only on that patch
Leave the side windows covered if the route is familiar
Use the defroster after entering heavy traffic instead
bank.why: DMV says clear the windows even for a short journey.

refs.section: Driving in Ice, Snow; Seasonal Driving

bank.q: Colorado: why should pedestrians and bicyclists receive additional winter clearance?
c: They may need to maneuver around snow or ice
They always have better traction than cars
They cannot legally use a winter roadway
They must stay motionless whenever a car approaches
bank.why: The winter page notes these necessary maneuvers.

refs.section: Driving in Ice, Snow; Seasonal Driving

bank.q: Colorado: what happens to stopping on a slippery road compared with a road with good grip?
c: Stopping distance always stays the same
Stopping becomes shorter once snow starts melting
bank.why: The page links reduced tire grip to longer stops.

refs.section: Driving in Ice, Snow; Seasonal Driving

bank.q: Colorado: winter tires or chains are fitted. Does that guarantee the vehicle cannot slip?
c: No; they can still slip on slick pavement
Yes; traction equipment prevents every skid
Yes, if the driver uses cruise control
Only high-speed travel can cause them to slip

topics.name: Connecticut lane and centerline markings
notes: White lane lines separate traffic traveling in the same direction; yellow centerlines separate opposing traffic.
Dashed white permits a lane change only when safe. A solid white lane line means remain in the lane unless a special situation requires changing.
With a solid yellow alongside a dashed yellow, passing is permitted only from the dashed side, subject to safe conditions.
A double solid yellow is not a passing invitation; the manual separately allows crossing it for specified left turns.

Marking before which a required stop is made

lessons.t: Read the color and pattern together
idea: A line pattern is not a guarantee of a safe gap.
recipe: Identify the conditions and conflicts.
Apply the rule or safety principle in the cited section.
Explain what to do and what could change the decision.

steps.text: Scenario: a dashed white line separates your lane from the next same-direction lane.

c: Lanes moving in the same direction
Traffic moving in opposite directions on every road

An immediate lane change without checking traffic
Passing through any intersection regardless of signs
Automatic priority over a vehicle in the other lane

bank.q: Connecticut: what does a solid white line between travel lanes generally tell you?
c: Stay in the lane unless a special situation requires changing
Opposing traffic is on the far side
The lane is reserved for parking only

bank.q: Connecticut: a solid yellow line and dashed yellow line form the centerline. You are next to the solid line. May you pass another vehicle across it?

Yes, if the vehicle ahead signals right

bank.q: Connecticut: what does a yellow centerline separate?

Only bus lanes from car lanes
The shoulder from the curb on every road

Yes; every legal crossing also permits overtaking
Yes, if the overtaken car is moving slowly
Only if the passing car is smaller

At the center of the intersection

bank.q: Connecticut: which edge-line color is described for the left edge of a divided roadway?
bank.why: The edge-line section distinguishes the divided-road left edge from the white right edge.

topics.name: Connecticut observation before changing lanes
notes: Check rear-view and side mirrors and make a brief shoulder check toward the intended movement.
Keep monitoring ahead rather than staring sideways. Check the far lane for a driver aiming at the same gap.
When crossing several lanes, move one lane at a time and reassess.
Merging from a ramp or joining from a curb or shoulder also requires checking the destination lane.
gloss: Area near the rear corners not visible through mirrors
Brief direct look toward the intended movement
Lane beyond the one you intend to enter
One lane change followed by a fresh assessment

lessons.t: Mirrors do not show every conflict
idea: A gap must be checked from more than one view.
recipe: Identify the conditions and conflicts.
Apply the rule or safety principle in the cited section.
Explain what to do and what could change the decision.

steps.text: Scenario: your mirrors show no car in the lane you intend to enter.

lessons.t: A destination gap can be shared by two drivers
idea: Look beyond the nearest lane before moving.
recipe: Identify the conditions and conflicts.
Apply the rule or safety principle in the cited section.
Explain what to do and what could change the decision.

steps.text: Scenario: you and a vehicle in the far lane may both be aiming for the middle lane.
Check the far lane and wait if the movements would conflict.

bank.q: Connecticut: your mirrors appear clear before a lane change. What additional check does the manual describe?

Only a glance at the dashboard

At a dark traffic signal with no visible lighted indication, reduce speed and prepare to yield to vehicles in or approaching the intersection.
A steady green still requires yielding to lawful intersection and crosswalk traffic.
An otherwise permitted red-light turn requires a full stop and a safe path; posted prohibitions and steady red arrows control.

Full stop followed by safe entry

Apply the principle in the cited state source.

recipe: Identify the road layout and conflicts.

Recheck conditions before moving.

bank.why: Flashing red is treated as a stop sign.

Ignore crossing traffic facing another color

Yield only if the pedestrian waves

topics.name: Delaware directional and flashing arrows
notes: Arrows apply only to the indicated direction. A steady red arrow prohibits that movement.

A green arrow still requires yielding to pedestrians and vehicles lawfully in the intersection.

Stop, then choose a safe turn gap

Apply the principle in the cited state source.
Recheck conditions before moving.
oops: Treating both red arrows as the same turn permission.
